cells.rationale: The threshold of 4.86 equals the last FRED DGS10 print (2026-11-06) and the Treasury par curve read 4.88 on 2026-11-09, so the start is about 2 basis points above the line with four trading days to go and a strict test (a tie at 4.86 is No). Five-observation changes were higher in 54.5% of pairs over the last year and 49.4% over 10 years, and a typical weekly move of 10 basis points or more makes this close to a coin flip with a slight edge from the 4.88 starting point and the October CPI (2026-11-10) following a 3.7% September inflation print and two hawkish FOMC dissents. I shade it back toward 50% because the six earlier 10-year questions in my record all resolved no while yields drifted down from about 5.3% and a tie counts against yes. Sources: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10 (2026-11-09), https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value_month=202611 (2026-11-09), https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/cpi.htm, https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm (2026-10-28).

note: Recorded before every entry's cutoff; scored as a separate method.
